channel.title: Social Media Today - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Social Media Today (socialmediatoday.com)

item.title: US Supreme Court declines to hear AI copyright case
item.description: The decision upheld a lower court ruling that artificial intelligence-generated content does not have the same legal protections as human-created work.

item.title: Concerns with third-party partner could derail LinkedIn’s verification push
item.description: The company has continued to add more identification checks and balances, but questions remain regarding its verification partner Persona.

item.title: Almost half of US consumers use TikTok as a search engine
item.description: The app’s use as a discovery tool is rising as users turn to its short-form videos and personalized content to find information, according to research from Adobe.

item.title: More teen social media bans are coming, but will they work?
item.description: While the world attempts to limit underage access to apps, teenagers continue to find new ways to bypass rules and undermine systems.

item.title: Meta updates ad metrics to align with other platforms
item.description: The changes include simplified link click attribution and new engagement metrics, which could impact how ad results are measured.

item.title: X invites users to beta test X Chat app
item.description: The separate tool will function similarly to Meta’s Messenger and will be linked to users’ main accounts.

item.title: Meta tests shopping AI chatbot in U.S.
item.description: The feature would allow users to request product recommendations, per Bloomberg, and is similar to functions being tested by Google and OpenAI.

item.title: X usage declined in the EU in the second half of 2025
item.description: The platform’s latest reporting showed a decline of nearly 15% since the first half of last year, though the company claims overall record numbers.

item.title: X to take action against AI deepfakes of the Iran conflict
item.description: Nikita Bier, the platform’s head of product, said users who don’t add AI disclosures will be suspended from Creator Revenue Sharing for at least 90 days.

item.title: Meta updates Edits app with more creation tools
item.description: The company’s development team added video effects and improved the Ideas tab while also bringing in new text elements.
